q: For an investor to get a quick sense of risk in a mutual fund scheme, SEBI mandates a simplified framework called:
e: Riskometer is the SEBI-mandated visual risk indicator on all scheme documents and advertisements.

q: How many levels does the Riskometer have?
e: Riskometer has 6 levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, Very High.

q: A mutual fund distributor is required to obtain:
e: Distributors must obtain an AMFI Registration Number (ARN) after passing NISM V-A and completing KYD.

q: EUIN stands for:
e: EUIN identifies the individual employee/relationship manager of the ARN-holder who advised the investor — enables accountability.

q: NISM V-A certification is valid for:
e: NISM V-A certification is valid for 3 years. CPE (Continuing Professional Education) renewal is required to extend.

q: For an MF distributor handling investor money, the requirement is:
o: Must be incorporated as a company
Cannot accept investor money in own bank account — must be paid to scheme account directly
e: Distributors must NEVER accept investor funds in their own account. Cheques/transfers must go directly to the scheme.

q: A fundamental attribute change to a scheme requires:
o: Notice + exit window without exit load
e: Fundamental attribute changes (investment objective, asset allocation, fees) require written notice AND a 30-day no-load exit window for investors.

q: Direct plans of mutual funds were introduced by SEBI in:
e: Direct plans were introduced on 1 January 2013. They exclude distributor commission and have lower TER.

q: AMFI Code of Conduct prohibits which of the following?
o: Comparing schemes within same category transparently
e: Distributors cannot promise/guarantee specific returns — mutual funds are subject to market risk. Code mandates fair, transparent dealings.

q: Trail commission is paid to the distributor:
o: Once at the time of investment
Every year as long as the investor holds units
e: Trail commission is recurring — paid as long as investor holds units. Aligns distributor incentive with investor retention. Upfront commissions banned for retail.

q: Scheme advertisements must include:
e: Mandatory: Riskometer, standard disclaimer ("Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks…"), and SID reference.

q: Which document gives the latest information about a scheme's portfolio, NAV, and AUM?
e: Monthly factsheet provides current snapshot — portfolio holdings, NAV, AUM, returns. SID is at scheme launch; KIM is summary of SID; SAI has statutory info.

q: Riskometer has how many levels?
e: 6 levels: Low to Very High.

q: NISM V-A certification validity:
e: 3 years; renewable via CPE.

q: EUIN identifies:
e: The individual employee/RM who advised the investor.

q: Fundamental attribute change requires:
e: Notice plus 30-day exit window without exit load.

q: The SEBI Regulation governing mutual funds in India is:
e: SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 (as amended over time) is the primary regulation. Indian Trusts Act, 1882 governs the trust structure separately.

q: Trail commission to a distributor:
o: Is paid only at the time of investment
Is paid as long as the investor stays invested
Is paid only if the fund beats benchmark
e: Trail commission accrues recurring as long as investor holds units, aligning distributor incentives with retention. Upfront commissions for retail are banned.

q: A distributor accepting investor cheques in their own bank account is:
o: Strictly prohibited under AMFI Code of Conduct
e: Distributors must NEVER take investor money in their own account. Funds must flow directly to the scheme account.

q: EUIN is required for:
o: Each individual employee/relationship manager who advises investors
e: EUIN identifies the individual employee/RM (within the ARN-holder firm) who advised the investor — enables accountability and prevents mis-selling claims.

q: Mutual funds can buy and sell securities only on a delivery basis. Is this true?
e: TRUE. Mutual funds can buy/sell securities only on delivery basis (no carry-forward / speculative trading on the same day) — to ensure investor protection and avoid speculation.

q: Regarding celebrity endorsements for mutual funds, SEBI has permitted:
o: Endorsement of individual mutual fund schemes
Celebrity endorsement at the industry level (for awareness only)
e: SEBI permits celebrity endorsement only at INDUSTRY level (for awareness, e.g., "Mutual Funds Sahi Hai") — not for promoting individual schemes.

q: The primary role of a mutual fund distributor is to:
o: Analyse the situation of the investor and recommend suitable schemes
e: Distributor analyses the INVESTOR (needs, goals, risk profile). Fund manager analyses the MARKET. Both work towards investor's financial goals.

q: Among the following, which is NOT a category of mutual fund distributor?
e: Stock exchanges are not distributors. Categories: Individual ARN holders, Corporate distributors (banks, NBFCs), National Distributors (large multi-state firms), Online platforms.

q: A distributor must complete which process before getting an ARN from AMFI?
o: Pass NISM V-A and complete KYD (Know Your Distributor)
e: Pass NISM V-A → Complete KYD (biometric, document verification) → Apply to AMFI for ARN. Without KYD, ARN cannot be issued.

q: An ARN issued by AMFI is valid for:
e: ARN is valid for 3 years. Renewal requires Continuing Professional Education (CPE) compliance.

q: When a distributor offers ONLY execution services (not advice), the EUIN field in the form should be:
o: Left blank with explicit declaration of execution-only
e: For execution-only transactions (no advice), EUIN field can be left blank with a signed declaration. This protects against future mis-selling claims.

q: Trail commission to distributors is paid:
o: Only at the time of investment
Annually as long as the investor holds units
e: Trail commission is recurring — paid (typically monthly) as long as investor stays invested. Aligns distributor incentive with investor retention.

q: AMFI Code of Conduct prohibits a distributor from:
e: Distributors cannot promise or guarantee returns — mutual fund investments are subject to market risks. Code requires fair, transparent dealings.

q: A distributor who has been suspended by AMFI for a regulatory violation:
o: Can continue distributing through a different ARN
Must surrender the ARN and stop all distribution activity
e: Suspension means the distributor cannot use the ARN. They must stop distribution activity until suspension is lifted. Continuing without authority is a regulatory offence.

q: Grievance redressal for mutual fund investors first goes to:
e: Investor must FIRST raise grievance with the AMC. If unresolved within 30 days, escalate to SEBI SCORES. SEBI is not the first port of call.

q: SCORES is:
o: SEBI Complaints Redress System — online platform for investor complaints
e: SCORES = SEBI Complaints Redress System. Online portal where investors can file grievances against listed entities and intermediaries when AMC fails to resolve in 30 days.

q: For online execution-only platforms (RIA-exempt distributors), they can offer:
o: Only execution-only transactions in direct plans
Both regular and direct plans with advice
e: Pure execution-only platforms can transact in direct plans only and cannot offer personalised advice. If advice is offered, RIA registration is required.

q: Mutual fund advertisements must include the standard warning:
o: "Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks. Read all scheme related documents carefully."
"Past returns are guaranteed in the future"
No warning needed if returns are below 10%
e: The mandatory disclaimer must appear in all MF marketing communication, advertisements, brochures, and SID/SAI/KIM documents.

q: A new SEBI rule mandates that distributors and intermediaries display their registered name and registration number:
o: On home page of social media handles AND at beginning of any video/content related to securities markets
e: Recent SEBI rule: registered name and number must appear prominently on social media home pages and at the beginning of all securities-related video/content uploaded by intermediaries.

q: Due diligence by AMC on distributors includes verification of:
o: Compliance history, certifications, past actions, references
e: AMC due diligence covers compliance/regulatory history, NISM/CPE certifications, past disciplinary actions, references — to ensure distributor fits AMFI Code of Conduct.

q: For mis-selling, AMFI Code of Conduct expects distributors to:
o: Be paid based on commission only
Match products to investor risk profile and document the rationale
e: Distributors must match products to risk profile and goals, document the rationale, and avoid pushing high-commission schemes regardless of suitability.

q: Investors' complaints filed via SCORES are typically expected to be resolved within:
e: SEBI requires resolution within 30 days from when the entity receives the complaint via SCORES.

q: AMFI Code of Conduct requires distributors to maintain confidentiality of:
e: Investor information, transaction details, and personal data must be kept confidential — used only for the intended purpose. Confidentiality is a core ethical obligation.

q: When a distributor changes (investor wishes to assign units to a new distributor), the procedure is:
o: The investor submits a Change of Distributor request to the AMC, which honours it without needing the existing distributor's consent
e: Investors can change distributors freely. AMC processes the request without requiring NOC from the existing distributor. New trail accrues to the new distributor going forward.

q: A distributor receiving an upfront commission for retail investors is:
o: Banned by SEBI for retail investors (only trail commission allowed)
e: Upfront commissions for retail investors are banned. Distributors get only trail commission for retail. (B-30 cities have a small upfront incentive in some categories, with conditions.)

q: EUIN identifies which entity within the distribution chain?
o: The individual employee/relationship manager who advised the investor
e: EUIN (Employee Unique Identification Number) identifies the specific employee/RM within the ARN-holder firm. Enables accountability for advice given.

q: A distributor accepting a personal cheque from an investor in their own name (for investing later) is:
o: Strictly prohibited under AMFI Code of Conduct
e: Accepting investor money in personal account is STRICTLY PROHIBITED. Investor funds must always flow directly to the scheme's collection account.

q: A distributor may receive commission for selling mutual funds, but they CANNOT charge investors:
o: Direct fees from the investor for distribution (only AMC pays them)
e: Distributors cannot charge investors directly for distribution. They are compensated only by the AMC via commission. RIAs (Registered Investment Advisers) are different and CAN charge fees directly.

q: Direct plans of mutual funds were introduced from:
e: Direct plans were introduced on 1 January 2013 — they exclude distribution commission and have lower TER, leading to higher net returns over time.

q: Difference between Distributor and Investment Advisor (RIA):
o: Distributor receives commission from AMC; RIA charges fees directly from clients and offers advice
RIA is below distributor in seniority
e: Distributor: AMC pays commission, primarily executes/facilitates. RIA: Fee from client, fiduciary advice. Different SEBI registrations and regulatory frameworks.

q: AMFI Code of Ethics requires members to observe high standards of:
o: Integrity and fairness in dealings with all stakeholders
e: AMFI Code of Ethics centres on integrity, fairness, transparency, fiduciary responsibility, and prioritising unitholder interests in all dealings.

q: AMFI requires distributors to keep records of investor transactions for at least:
e: Distributors must maintain investor transaction records for at least 5 years — standard SEBI/AMFI requirement, though specific retention may vary by transaction type.

q: As per SEBI regulations, a mutual fund scheme/plan must have a minimum of __ investors:
e: SEBI requires every scheme/plan to have a minimum of 20 investors. This is the "20-25 rule".

q: No single investor in a mutual fund scheme can hold more than __ of the corpus of the scheme/plan:
e: No single investor can hold more than 25% of the corpus. Together with the 20-investor minimum, this is the "20-25 rule" preventing concentration.

q: If the 20-investor minimum or the 25% concentration limit is breached, the AMC must:
o: Refund the entire corpus to investors
Rebalance within a SEBI-prescribed cure period or wind up
e: AMC must rebalance to comply within a SEBI-prescribed cure period (typically a calendar quarter). If unable to cure, scheme must be wound up and money returned.

q: A first-time mutual fund investor making an investment of ₹10,000 or above through a distributor — the transaction charge deducted and paid to the distributor is:
e: For NEW investors, transaction charge of ₹150 per transaction (₹10,000 or above) is deducted from the investment and paid to the distributor. The balance is invested.

q: For an EXISTING mutual fund investor (already invested with any AMC) making a transaction of ₹10,000 or above through a distributor, the transaction charge is:
e: For EXISTING investors, transaction charge is ₹100 per transaction (₹10,000 or above), deducted from investment and paid to the distributor.

q: No transaction charge is applicable on:
o: Direct plans / investments below ₹10,000 / SIPs where total investment is below ₹10,000
e: Transaction charges DO NOT apply to: (a) Direct plans, (b) Investments below ₹10,000, (c) SIPs where total commitment is below ₹10,000, (d) Switches.

q: A mutual fund scheme can lend up to __ of its net assets in stock lending, subject to specific conditions:
e: A scheme can lend a maximum of 20% of its net assets to a single approved intermediary, subject to overall lending caps and SEBI conditions.

q: Empanelment of a distributor with an AMC — typically:
o: Is permanent and cannot be terminated
Can be terminated by the AMC at any time as per the empanelment declaration signed
Can be terminated only by SEBI
e: On empanelment, the distributor signs a declaration giving the AMC the right to terminate empanelment at any time (e.g., for breach of code, regulatory action, conduct issues).

q: A distributor whose ARN has expired can:
o: Continue selling for one grace year
Not transact (no new business) — but trail commission on existing AUM continues till lapse
e: If ARN lapses (no CPE renewal), the distributor cannot solicit new business. Trail commission on existing AUM may continue per AMC policy until specific lapse rules trigger.

q: Mutual fund schemes can buy and sell securities only on:
e: Mutual funds can transact only on DELIVERY basis (no carry-forward / speculative trading). This protects unitholders from speculative risk.

q: A scheme advertisement claiming guaranteed returns:
o: Is strictly prohibited unless backed by sponsor guarantee disclosed in SID
Is permitted only for liquid funds
Is allowed in B-30 cities only
e: Guaranteed returns can be claimed ONLY if explicitly backed by a sponsor guarantee disclosed in the SID. Otherwise prohibited under SEBI advertisement code.

q: SEBI's advertisement code prohibits mutual fund ads from:
o: Using forward-looking statements like "guaranteed double in 5 years"
e: Forward-looking unrealistic claims, guarantees of returns, or projections without basis are prohibited. Past performance with disclaimers and Riskometer are required.

q: Past performance disclosure rule: scheme returns must be shown for periods of:
e: Standard disclosure: 1-year, 3-year, 5-year, and since-inception returns alongside benchmark returns for the same periods.

q: The "Mutual Funds Sahi Hai" campaign is an example of:
e: Industry-level investor awareness campaigns (where celebrities can be used) are permitted. Individual scheme/AMC celebrity endorsement is NOT permitted.

q: AMFI Code of Ethics centres on:
o: Integrity, fairness, and prioritising unitholder interests
e: AMFI Code of Ethics: integrity, fairness, fiduciary responsibility to unitholders, transparency, conflict-of-interest avoidance, ethical conduct in all dealings.

q: A potential conflict of interest at AMC level — for example, if AMC employees personally trade in stocks held by schemes — is governed by:
o: Personal trading / front-running prohibitions in SEBI regulations and AMC code
e: SEBI strictly prohibits personal trading by AMC employees in scheme-held securities (front-running). AMCs must have policies, surveillance, and pre-clearance systems.

q: The SEBI Investor Charter for Mutual Funds covers:
o: Investor rights, redressal mechanisms, expected service standards, list of dos and don'ts
e: Investor Charter (mandated by SEBI) lists investor rights, expected service standards from AMCs, grievance redressal processes, and red flags. Must be prominently displayed.

q: A distributor making personal social media posts about mutual fund schemes must:
o: Display registered name and ARN at the start of the content + comply with AMFI/SEBI ad code
Get SEBI pre-approval for each post
e: Recent SEBI rule: registered name + registration number must appear prominently on social media handles and at the start of any video/content related to securities.

q: AMCs must disclose distributor commissions paid:
o: Quarterly on AMC website (top distributors named with commissions paid)
e: AMCs must disclose top distributor commissions quarterly on their website — commission disclosure norms enforce transparency on distribution costs.

q: The "Fit and Proper" criteria for empanelling distributors include:
o: Adequate controls to delink sales functions from customer risk/objective evaluation, regulatory history, references
e: Due diligence by AMCs covers structural controls (delinking sales from suitability assessment), regulatory record, NISM/CPE certifications, references, conduct history.

q: A distributor who has been suspended by AMFI for code violations:
o: Can register a new ARN to bypass
Must surrender ARN privileges and stop distribution; suspension is publicly disclosed
e: AMFI publicly maintains records of suspended/terminated ARNs. Suspended distributors cannot transact through any ARN. Bypassing via fresh ARN is not permitted.

q: For an AMC employee who is also an active investor in their own AMC's schemes:
o: Permitted with mandatory disclosures and pre-clearance per AMC's personal trading policy
e: Personal investments by AMC employees are allowed but governed by mandatory disclosure and pre-clearance policies — to prevent front-running and conflicts.

q: For a New Fund Offer (NFO) — celebrity endorsement is:
o: Strictly prohibited (only industry-level awareness via celebrities is allowed)
e: Individual scheme / NFO celebrity endorsement is strictly prohibited. Celebrity use is allowed ONLY at industry-level awareness campaigns.

q: Past performance disclosure in scheme advertisements must show returns for:
o: 1, 3, 5 years and since inception (alongside benchmark for same periods)
e: Standard disclosure: 1Y/3Y/5Y/SI returns + benchmark TRI for same periods. Forward-looking projections prohibited.

q: AMC must disclose top distributor commissions on:
e: SEBI commission disclosure norms require AMCs to publicly disclose top distributors and commissions paid — quarterly on the website. Promotes transparency.

q: The ARN (AMFI Registration Number) of a distributor is valid for:
e: ARN valid for 3 years. Distributor must complete CPE (Continuing Professional Education) to renew.

q: A scheme must have a minimum of __ investors and no single investor can hold more than __ of the corpus:
e: SEBI 20-25 rule: minimum 20 investors; no single investor more than 25%. Cure period for breach; if not cured, scheme must wind up.

q: Distributors registered with AMFI must complete which due diligence step before getting ARN?
e: Pass NISM V-A → Complete KYD (biometric, document verification) → Apply to AMFI for ARN.

q: The "Investor Charter" mandated by SEBI for mutual funds:
o: Lists investor rights, expected service standards, grievance redressal mechanisms, dos and don'ts
e: Investor Charter: lists rights, expected service standards from AMCs, grievance redressal, complaint escalation. Must be prominently displayed.
